title: Prune cuobj bloat and introduce lightweight kernel manifest for faster startup
creator: Lena Park
description: Background: Recent runtime audits show a consistent cold-start regression caused by large cuobj (.cubin/.ptx) bundles being pulled into the process at initialization. These bundles include rarely-used kernels and multiple CUTLASS variants that are only needed for a subset of models, which increases symbol resolution time, ld.so overhead, and memory churn during warmup. The goal of this ticket is twofold: (1) implement a deterministic, lightweight kernel manifest that enumerates only the kernels required by a model profile and (2) add a safe prune-and-validate flow to strip unused cuobj binaries from runtime images and during boxed model onboarding. This should reduce cold-start startup time, kernel probe jitter, and lower image sizes for Dedicated/Private deploys.
proposal:
- Add a serialized kernel-manifest format (versioned) that the serving runtime can consult at startup to restrict immediate kernel registration to a minimal working set. Manifests are generated by the build/onboarding step and attached to model bundles.
- Implement a runtime 'manifest gating' option (default off for older releases) that defers loading of non-manifest cuobj sections until first use.
- Add a CI job that validates prune correctness by running a small smoke-model matrix and comparing numeric outputs and kv-cache behavior.
- Provide a one-click pruning helper in the model onboarding CLI that creates a pruned artifact and a verification report for audits.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start p95 kernel-probe time reduced by >=25% on heterogeneous GPU nodes compared to baseline-2026-02
Model functional parity: numeric diffs between pruned and unpruned artifacts within existing eval thresholds for 95% of selected prompt suite
Automated rollback: if a pruned bundle fails verification in ~10% of system runs, runtime auto-falls back to full-cuobj mode for that bundle and emits a telemetry event
CI regression job integrated into pre-merge checks for runtime and model-onboarding repos
Documentation: Confluence runbook describing manifest format, prune heuristics, and emergency rollback procedure
tasks: Design kernel-manifest schema (fields: model-id, kernel-hash, required-kernel-list, compatibility-tags, manifest-version)
Instrument build/onboard pipeline to record actual kernel usage via sandboxed inference runs and produce initial manifests
Implement runtime manifest loader and gated cuobj resolver with a controlled feature-flag
Add verification harness for numeric parity and KV-cache integrity tests
Add a pruning CLI command and create a 'prune-report' artifact (contains diff, tests passed, warnings)
Add Grafana dashboards and telemetry for manifest misses, fallback counts, and startup latencies
Write migration notes for Dedicated/Private teams and create a small canary rollout plan
risks: False negative pruning that removes a kernel used only in rare edge-case prompts -> mitigated by conservative heuristics and fallback mode
Increased complexity in the model onboarding CI and longer artifact build times -> mitigate by parallelizing sandbox runs and caching manifests
Compatibility with older runtime versions that expect full cuobj sets -> provide feature-flag and server-side rollout gating
Potential SLO regressions during canary if manifest generation is incorrect; require short canary windows and rapid rollback path
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser and gated loader (CI coverage >= 95%)
Integration tests: run pruned vs unpruned artifacts across 5 model families and verify token-level regressions under threshold
Performance tests: nightly regression benchmark measuring cold-start 50/95/99p on standard heterogeneous fleet
Canary: enable manifest gating for 5% of traffic in a dedicated pool with extra tracing enabled for 48 hours
Add synthetic failure injection that simulates missing kernel loads and verify fallback behavior and telemetry events
progress_comments: 2026-02-26 - Lena Park: Kicked off design spike. Ran binary inspection against 120 model bundles; average cuobj overhead ~18MB per model. Noted several duplicate CUTLASS variants across model families.
2026-03-02 - Miguel Santos: Prototype manifest loader implemented in runtime branch 'manifest-gate'. Initial local runs show 22% reduction in kernel probe p95 on T4 nodes.

2026-03-05 - QA (Ravi Patel): Built verification harness. Found two model families where pruning removed a fallback kernel needed for fp16->int8 transpose path. Updated heuristic to detect lib-call sites during sandbox runs.
2026-03-09 - Miguel Santos: Opened onboarding CLI PR with pruning command and added 'prune-report' JSON output. Added integration test stubs to model-onboard CI.
2026-03-12 - Product (Aisha Kapoor): Reviewed canary plan and approved 5% traffic pilot with 48h telemetry window. Requested additional dashboard tile for 'manifest.missed_kernels' metric.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive pruning reduces startup but increases chance of fallback; we choose conservative pruning by default and expose opt-in aggressive profile for Dedicated customers who accept risk.
Long-term: consider splitting monolithic cuobj bundles into micro-bundles keyed by capability tags so runtime can lazy-load fewer bytes on first use.
Coordination: Need infra assistance for adding new s3 lifecycle policy for prune reports and a transient bucket for canary artifacts.
